The largest electromagnetic force in the melt appears near the solid-liquid interface.
There are intensive electromagnetic vibrations in front of the solid-liquid interface.
The forced melt convection is mainly concentrated in front of the solid-liquid interface, with a larger flow velocity.
The maximum electromagnetic force in the melt is around 3.6 x 10^4 N/m^3.
The flow velocity along the thermal gradient in front of the solid-liquid interface is greater than 2 mm/s.
The forced convection homogenizes the temperature field in the melt, reducing the temperature gradient ahead of the solidification front.
The criterion for dendrite fragmentation is when the component of flow velocity along the thermal gradient (u_l,z) becomes larger than the speed of the isotherms (V_T), i.e. u_l,z/V_T > 1.
The pulse frequency of the pulsed magnetic field is 5 Hz.
The peak current density in the coil of the pulsed magnetic field is 3 x 10^7 A/m^2.
The withdrawal speed of the sample during directional solidification is 0.75 mm/s.
The Joule heat in the solid phase is significantly higher than that in the liquid phase.
The Joule heat in the ascending stage is greater than that in the descending stage.
The grain structure of the superalloy K4169 changes from columnar to fine equiaxed grains with the application of the pulsed magnetic field.
The electromagnetic vibration and forced convection in front of the solid-liquid interface are the main reasons for the grain refinement.
The solid-liquid interface tends to be flatter with the application of the pulsed magnetic field.
